newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi wants pension reform impact studied.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi wants pension reform impact studied.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi on Wednesday asked a special body monitoring pension spending to expand its role and to carry out a study of the impact of potential changes to current regulations.
Prodi's office said in a statement that he asked for the change in a meeting with Labour Minister Tiziano Treu.
The request appeared to be a first step towards a review of last year's pension reform deal that Prodi has said will begin next year, rather than in 1998 as originally planned.
Treu said earlier this week the centre-left government intended to begin a review of last year's pension reform deal in 1997, confirming similar comments by Prodi last week.

Trade union leaders, backed by the hard left Communist Refoundation party that ensures the government's majority in parliament, have fiercely rejected suggestions that the revision should be brought forward.
Analysts have criticised the 1995 pension reform, enacted by then prime minister Lamberto Dini, for being too slow in moving to eradicate generous early retirement packages.

Commentators have said Italy needs to restructure pensions spending to balance its books and get the ratio between the state deficit and gross domestic product below the three- percent level needed to join Europe's planned single currency.
